summary: Bashar al-Assad, a London-trained eye doctor who inherited Syria's dictatorship in 2000, crushed the 2011 uprising with torture prisons, barrel bombs and chemical weapons, killing hundreds of thousands of Syrians.
keywords: Vogue profile A Rose in the Desert

evidence.note: Birth in September 1965 opens the biography
Works as an ophthalmologist at a London hospital before being recalled
Hafez dies June 2000 and Bashar takes power after a constitutional change
Damascus Spring reforms and their reversal with arrests and a press law
CIA rendition of detainees to Syrian torture prisons, Maher Arar case
Arar seized at JFK airport by US authorities and sent to Syria
Long segment on the paid-for Vogue puff piece about Asma al-Assad
Daraa schoolboys arrested for graffiti, protests spread in 2011
Bouazizi self-immolation recounted as the Arab Spring trigger
Barrel bombing of Homs and Aleppo, hospitals and schools targeted
Obama White House backs away from enforcing the chemical weapons red line
Ongoing bombing of Idlib at release supports reaches_present

notes: Alive and in power at release, so main_span ends null and covered_span ends 2019. Hafez's 1963-1982 rise and Hama get brief background, so covered_span starts at Bashar's birth. A several-minute segment rebuts chemical-weapon false-flag claims; conspiracy-theories left out to keep themes focused. Tunisia (Bouazizi) is Arab Spring context and is not in setting.
